paragraphs.source_en: survives from the reign of Constantine in the east is an oration celebrating the thirteenth anniversary of his rule. It was preached by none other than Eusebios of Kaisareia. Constantine, he says, prevailed over Licinius through the sign of the Cross, which he has erected in the imperial City “as a talisman to safeguard the empire of the Romans and his imperial rule over all.” The ideal of Christian peace had yielded to traditional notions of Roman imperial victory.38 With surprising ease, Christianity became an instrument for bolstering loy- alty to the empire. In every church, whether in the capital or an insignificant vil- lage, worship ended with a prayer on behalf of the empire, the emperor, and his subjects.
